title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
lede: G2 Venture Partners' Brook Porter argues that solar paired with long-duration storage, not natural gas, is the fastest way to power the next wave of AI data centers.

points: Porter puts yearly global gas capacity at about 60 to 70 gigawatts, against well over a terawatt for solar.
Solar and most long-duration storage are small modular units, so they get cheaper with volume, the effect known as Wright's Law.
G2VP, which led Crusoe's Series C, expects data center investment above $4 trillion through the end of the decade.
The firm sees two paths: small on-grid sites with their own generation, and large off-grid sites on solar and storage.
Storage from Form Energy and G2VP-backed Antora Energy has cut cost per megawatt-hour well below lithium-ion.

sections.text: Off-grid renewable sites could sidestep grid connection queues and air permits, so where and how fast new compute comes online would depend less on the grid.
